answer: Borrow Bryan Ford's pseudonym parties. Quarterly, operators attend venues that all open in the same hour worldwide; each gets one token, its quartz-clock issue time inside that hour, since no one stands in two rooms at once. Agents earn only when bound to a token, and one token's n agents split sqrt(n) shares: illustratively, a reef of 100 clones earns 10, not 100. Bribed attendees evade it at about a day's wage each, and a crooked host behind a velvet curtain could over-issue, so a random second witness recounts each room. Honest fleets lose some pay; remote operators need a video lane.
